newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover soars in week to Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover soars in week to Oct 11.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 21.37 percent rise in its turnover during the week ending October 11.
Total weekly turnover jumped to 30.823 million dinars ($6.1 million) from 25.395 million dinars a week earlier. The number of transactions inched higher to 162 from 156.

Traders said a persistent lack of fresh funds was still slowing down market activity. "Investors are withdrawing their funds in order to meet other liabilities -- to pay salaries for example," one trader said.
Tight liquidity was also reflected in rising interest rates, analysts said.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills moved higher, ranging between 331 and 793 percent a year. They stood between an annual 44 and 644 percent a week ago.
The BSE turnover was dominated by the commercial paper segment with 140 deals worth 16.578 million dinars.
Central bank short-term bonds were traded four times for a volume of 11.25 million dinars.
The bourse reported 17 deals in treasury bills worth 2.695 million dinars.
There was no trade in wheat selling forward contracts. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
